podcast.body: One year after Prince and the Revolution's imperial run with "Purple Rain," this electro-funk jam from Flint, Michigan's Ready for the World topped the Hot 100 in 1985. Many pop fans "mistook for Prince," demonstrating the imperial artist's influence on imitators' success. "Ready for the World, topped the Hot 100 with an electro-funk jam, O'Sheela, that many pop fans mistook for Prince."

podcast.body: This number one smash by the Minneapolis Synth Funk band opened with a spoken-word bit by lead singer Melvin Riley Jr. that "approximated a faux-British accent," which felt like a "troll" similar to 60s American bands like The Raiders or The Sir Douglas Quintet. "In late 85, the Minneapolis Synth Funk band, Ready for the World, opened their number one smash O'Shila with a spoken word bit by lead singer Melvin Riley Jr. that approximated a faux-British accent."
